I need it. After last week's picks, I need to go into hiding. It was awful. When you can't get over .500 with the straight-up picks, you know it's a bad week. I went 6-8 straight up and 3-11 against the spread. I could flip a coin and do better. Maybe my cats will make my picks next week. My season records are now 54-38-1 straight up and 37-54-2 against the spread. That is vile. Time to turn it around, so I am going to the dogs. Let them bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. Pick: Cowboys 21, Eagles 20 Now Playing Share Share Video Prisco's Week 7 picks: Patriots upset Bears, Lions edge Packers Can anyone take control of the NFC East? Who makes the playoffs? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. The New England Patriots suffered a pair of concerning injury setbacks during Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets , with two former New York starters exiting against their old team. Right tackle Morgan Moses and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker both sustained injuries during the Oct. 18 AFC East showdown at Gillette Stadium. Shortly afterward, Reiss reported another Patriots injury announcement , this time involving Vera-Tucker. The developments created an unusual storyline for New England, considering both players previously held starting roles with the Jets before making their way to the Patriots. The veteran previously started 16 games for the Jets in 2021 before returning for a second stint in 2024, when he made 14 starts at right tackle. He subsequently signed a three-year, $24 million contract with the Patriots and became a fixture along their offensive line. Moses started all 17 regular-season games and four playoff contests in 2025, providing much-needed stability for New England's offensive front. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. Bears are 2nd-best team in the NFC when healthy Contact/Follow @TrojansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of USC Trojans news, notes and opinion. home.headline: Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five players for Thursday Night Football vs. the Bears
home.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five players for Thursday Night Football vs. the Bears Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS The Patriots ruled out CB Carlton Davis III (neck), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), G Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring) for Thursday night in Chicago. On Wednesday, the Patriots ruled out LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots are also listing RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder), and LB Christian Ellliss (chest) as questionable for Thursday night's game. Starting on offense, the Patriots offensive line will be shorthanded, with the Pats down multiple guards who have started games this season. Along with starting RG Mike Onwenu (ankle) and top backup Greg Van Roten (thigh), who are on injured reserve, New England is also down Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Brown (knee). In his final press conference before Thursday night's game, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will start vs. the Bears. The Pats projected starting offensive line is LT Will Campbell, LG Walter Rouse, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses (questionable) or Caleb Lomu. If Moses can't finish the game and the Patriots start Lomu at guard, the rookie would need to kick back outside. Vrabel also hinted at Lomu being prepared to be the backup center. In short, that's a lot of moving parts to plan for in-game contingencies, so the clearest path forward is to start Rouse and Pryor at guard while Lomu continues in his role as the top swing tackle. Plus, Moses is listed as questionable, and if he doesn't play on the short week, Lomu would make his first NFL start at right tackle. At the skill positions, the Patriots are down two wide receivers, Doubs and Hollins, both on injured reserve. However, the Pats will have top WR A.J. Brown, whose ankle is off the injury report. New England's available wideouts are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III, while OC Josh McDaniels can use all his tight ends and running backs. The Patriots could elevate a fifth wide receiver from the practice squad, but that feels unlikely with limited game-day roster spots. Moving over to the defense, starting CB Carlton Davis III (neck) will need to wait at least another week before returning to the lineup. Despite practicing in a limited capacity this week, Davis won't play on Thursday night, marking the third straight game he has missed with his neck injury (four out of the last six). The Patriots held lighter walkthrough sessions during a short week to prepare for the Bears, so Davis may have participated as a ramp-up for a potential return sooner rather than later. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a nearly disastrous loss to the New York Giants, the New Orleans Saints are facing another must-win situation against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the game will be played overseas in Paris. In that Week 6 game, the Saints' rookies put on some nice performances, and Week 7 may be the breakout game for this class. WR Jordyn Tyson Finally, we can talk about Jordyn Tyson. Although his availability for Sunday's game is up in the air, he did travel with the team, which means there's a chance he plays. The Saints' offense has had a number of issues this season, and although Tyson will not fix everything, he is a massive upgrade over Bryce Lance. The injuries have been demoralizing, to say the least, but Tyson is an extremely talented player who can be one of the best WRs in the NFL. Although I would expect a small sample size if he does play, we may finally see him on the field. DT Christen Miller Although this was another game where the Saints went with other DT options over Miller, he did get on the field and helped shut down New York's running game. In Week 7, the Saints face a much better rushing attack led by Jaylen Warren, so they will have to rely on Miller a bit more. TE Oscar Delp Against the Giants, Delp had his best game so far. He made some really important blocks that significantly helped the run game and had two catches. It wasn't an incredible performance by any means, but one that could lead to more snaps for Delp. Delp is likely going to be in the same exact role for Week 7. OG Jeremiah Wright After Cesar Ruiz left the game with an injury, rookie Jeremiah Wright was thrown into the lineup, and suddenly the run game looked great. Could this be a coincidence? Maybe. But it was clear that lanes were being opened up that the running backs could easily take advantage of. He got pushed back and beat at times, any rookie would, but overall, it was exactly what you wanted to see in his first real game. Now with Ruiz's health in question, and the fact Wright's debut was positve, the Saints must start him in Week 7. Might as well see what you have with Wright in a full game. WR Bryce Lance This was an up-and-down game for Lance. He once again had some head-scratching moments, including a drop, but he also scored the first touchdown of his young career. With Tyson's return, Lance may be demoted to a more blocking role, but that may be better for now, especially as he develops. WR Barion Brown I thought Barion Brown had the best game of his career as well. He had some really nice returns and made a nice contested catch that may have been an interception if he didn't get to the ball. Brown will likely fall to WR5 on the depth chart, but just like Lance, that's perfectly fine. RB CJ Donaldson Another up-and-down game, Donaldson had some really nice runs to begin the game and fought for some tough yards. He nearly scored the first touchdown of his career, but was called back after his knee was down short. His blocking was also good, which was needed against the blitzes. Then we get to the fumble. The Giants' comeback started after Donaldson fumbled, and that put a stain on this performance. Not sure if Donaldson will see fewer snaps in Week 7, but it's something to monitor. OT Mason Murphy Murphy did not come into this game like last week, but after Asim Richards clear struggles against the Giants, it may be time for New Orleans to try something new. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was once again an impact player on special teams, which is exactly why the Saints drafted him.

away.headline: Steelers face tough decisions on TJ Watt, Alex Highsmith as NFL trade deadline looms
away.blurb: Herbig is 24 and profiles as a long-term piece of the puzzle with 18 sacks in limited snaps across his first four NFL season. Veteran Maquez Valdes-Scantling was signed to the practice squad this week after finishing the season with the Steelers a year ago, but it’s possible Khan may want to give Rodgers a more serious option who’s currently on an NFL roster. Valdes-Scantling caught just 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown in five games with Pittsburgh last season, so his ability to make a major impact now is likely limited. From the moment Nick Herbig signed his four-year, $100 million extension in the offseason, the Pittsburgh Steelers’ future at outside linebacker has been a major question facing general manager Omar Khan. Now, with the NFL trade deadline looming on Nov. 10, he has a layered decision to make about whether to keep the highly paid trio of Herbig, T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith together for the duration of 2026 or deal one of them to bolster the current team’s depth or secure valuable draft capital for the future. The team’s recent hot streak has made a trade hard to fathom. The Steelers are tied with the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns for first in the AFC North division at 4-2. They’ve won three of their past four games as coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers have started to find consistent success with their short and quick passing game. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. Required reading: Dani Watt, wife of Steelers star T.J. Watt, questions NFL plan for Paris game Defensively, the Steelers have been solid against the pass. Only six teams are allowing fewer than the Steelers’ average of 204.3 yards per game through the air. The pass rush, which ranks ninth with 16 sacks, has helped the defensive backs win consistently on the outside. Watt, Highsmith and Herbig have accounted for 9.5 of those sacks. And Watt, of course, is one of the league’s most decorated players in terms of resume with 119.5 career sacks and a Defensive Player of the Year award on his trophy shelf. It makes sense reflexively not to mess with that kind of success. Then again, it also would have made short- and long-term sense to sign Joey Porter Jr. for the long term to bolster the secondary even further and strengthen the team for this season, which Rodgers has indicated will be his last in the NFL before heading off to likely Hall of Fame enshrinement. Instead, Khan opted not to sign Porter and traded him to the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 1. That move sent a message that the Steelers aren’t betting their whole strategy on Rodgers’ final season, even as they’d certainly like to make the playoffs and potentially make a deep run with him while they still can. It’s therefore natural to wonder if a similar calculation could be made that one of the outside linebackers is expendable for the right price. Will the Steelers trade a linebacker? Of the three, Highsmith seems most likely to move.

away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. away.blurb: Steelers Injury Central: 3 Out, 5 Questionable vs. Buccaneers Opens in a new tab Steelers News Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. away.headline: 49ers linked to Pro Bowl pass-rusher amid mounting injury issues
away.blurb: Bosa can return any week now, but the 49ers have been bracing to be without him for several weeks after he suffered a calf injury during warm-ups a few weeks ago. “Considering how important pressure is in the modern NFL, especially against the elite passers teams inevitably come up against in the playoffs, the Niners would be wise to bolster their edge-rushing unit with one of the best available free agents: Joey Bosa. The San Francisco 49ers may just be the best team in the NFL , but their mounting injury issues will catch up to them eventually. The team’s wide receiver corps has been ravaged in recent weeks with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Demarcus Robinson all going down with various ailments. The defensive side of the ball has also been hit hard by the injury bug as well. Defensive tackles Alfred Collins, CJ West, Sam Okuayinonu, edge-rushers Nick Bosa and Mikail Kamara, linebackers Nick Martin and Garret Wallow, cornerback Nate Hobbs, and safeties Marques Sigle and Darrick Forest are all either on injured reserve or have missed several weeks with their respective injuries. In the meantime, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay believes San Francisco should add to its pass-rush pool by signing a five-time Pro Bowler who’s quite familiar with one of the team’s top players. “While San Francisco features a top-five defense, it hasn’t generated pressure on a consistent basis,” Kay wrote . “An extended absence from top edge-rusher Nick Bosa — who has been dealing with a calf injury since Week 2 — has hindered the team’s ability to get after opposing quarterbacks. “… Even at the age of 31 with a history of injury, Joey Bosa can still be a force. He tallied five sacks, nine tackles for a loss, 16 quarterback hits and a league-leading five forced fumbles in 15 games with the Buffalo Bills last year and could be a key rotational piece for San Francisco in the back half of 2026.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported weeks ago that Joey Bosa was leaning toward retirement, but that doesn’t mean he can’t be tempted to play again in the right situation. Playing with his brother on a Super Bowl frontrunner where he won’t be relied on to play every down could be that perfect storm of temptation for him. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: How did enigmatic coach B.J. Callaghan lead Nashville SC atop MLS? | Exclusive News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 21, 2026, 5:07 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans are seeking their first consecutive win since 2022 after a victory over the Indianapolis Colts. Tennessee's offense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game, and quarterback Cam Ward had career lows in his last outing. Can the Tennessee Titans win twice in a row? That’s no small feat for an organization that hasn’t won consecutive games since 2022. But Tennessee’s 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts in NFL Week 6 quieted the storm after an 0-5 start. Now, the Titans (1-5) can prove it wasn’t a fluke when it hosts the Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Nissan Stadium on Oct. 25 (noon CT, CBS). The Browns are 1.5-point favorites. They lost last year's meeting 31-29 after Tennessee running back Tony Pollard rushed for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdowns. Questions remain for quarterback Cam Ward and the Titans' offense, who were bailed out by the defense and special teams against the Colts . Ward’s 11 completions and 102 yards passing against the Colts were career lows, and Tennessee still ranks last in the NFL in yards per game (236.3) and tied for last in points per game (14.0). Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cleveland Browns stat to know Other than the Baltimore Ravens ’ opening touchdown drive last week, the Browns surrendered three points and 169 yards of total offense to finish a 13-10 victory. Cleveland hasn’t been atop the AFC North this late in the season since 2014. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Browns Tennessee spent offseason resources beefing up its pass rush for coach Robert Saleh’s defensive scheme. The results finally surfaced with six sacks and 25 pressures against the Colts. Doing that again could hamper quarterback Deshaun Watson and the Browns, who have surrendered a league-high 24 sacks in six games. Cleveland left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber are both rookies. Titans eighth-year veteran Jeffery Simmons is arguably the NFL’s best defensive tackle. He has a team-high four sacks and 26 hurries. Where Cleveland Browns have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s passing offense is the NFL’s worst at 153.5 yards per game, and the Browns rank eighth in passing defense at 205.2 yards per game. Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward anchors a Cleveland secondary that ranks sixth in coverage grade at 71.1, according to Pro Football Focus. Cornerback Myles Harden has five passes defended this season. The Titans likely won’t win another game with a blocked punt return and four second-half field goals like they did against the Colts. If the Browns limit Cam Ward’s explosive plays downfield — they had six pass breakups against the Ravens — then Tennessee will struggle to score. Cam Ward has developed a go-to target in rookie receiver Carnell Tate, which is good. But receivers beyond Tate (44 targets) and Wan’Dale Robinson (37) aren’t that involved. Running back Tyjae Spears has more targets (17) than receiver Calvin Ridley (five). Elic Ayomanor has shown flashes of playmaking, but he’s averaging two targets the past four games and had a bad drop against the Colts. Score prediction: Browns 21, Titans 10 Ward’s limitations are clear through six games, giving Cleveland’s secondary a near-perfect blueprint. If nothing pops for Tennessee’s offense, the scoring woes will continue. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. An NFL spokesperson told The Tennessean on Oct. 21 that the Titans "promptly" notified the league about the matter, and it is under review. home.headline: Browns’ Latest Injury Update Raises Concerns Ahead of Titans Matchup
home.blurb: The Cleveland Browns are missing several notable players from practice ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . Camryn Justice of News 5 reported on six total players expected to be out for Wednesday practice: Delpit would be a big miss for the Browns, with one interception, one sack, and 25 combined tackles this year. Luckily for the Browns, they added depth at safety in the draft, and rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to emerge in recent weeks, with 24 tackles and just two receptions allowed this season. The Browns have some insurance at the position while Delpit works toward a return. Carson Schwesinger has been a defensive star for the Browns this season. Unfortunately, Schwesinger has been dealing with an ankle injury in recent weeks. The injury kept him out of practice most of last week ahead of the Ravens matchup, and he was limited in Friday's final practice. With Schwesinger missing Wednesday's practice, the Browns appear to be taking a similar approach this week. However, if his performance against the Ravens is any indication, Schwesinger should be available against the Titans. #Browns DT Mason Graham continued practicing today as he aims to return this week from the MCL sprain and ankle sprain he sustained in Week 4. pic.twitter.com/fSpap4sJZ2 Browns’ Latest Injury Update Raises Concerns Ahead of Titans Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM #Browns players not expected to practice today due to injury: Kalia Davis (quad) Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) Elgton Jenkins (knee) Teven Jenkins (back) Carson Schwesinger (ankle) Grant Delpit is one of the Browns' key defensive players and was injured after being accidentally struck by teammate Derek Barnett during a tackle attempt on Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Delpit is listed as having a shoulder injury as well as a concussion. Grant Delpit Took A Hard Hit To The Head As He Was Going In For The Tackle. This Definitely Does Not Look Good. Hope He’s All Good. Scary Moment. 😬 pic.twitter.com/u3VMCaBu40 Delpit is the most uncertain name on the Browns' injury report, as he sustained the concussion during Sunday's matchup against Baltimore. The NFL's concussion protocol can be difficult to navigate, and his absence from Wednesday's practice raises questions about his availability this Sunday. Elgton Jenkins has anchored the Browns' offensive line at center this season and has been a bright spot for the position group. Jenkins was listed with a knee injury ahead of Wednesday's practice after playing every offensive snap against the Ravens in Week 6. While his absence is worth monitoring, Jenkins' ability to play through last week's matchup is encouraging. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday. It seems like every week a big favorite is being upset, and Week 6 had two of them as the Los Angeles Rams (12.5-point favorites) lost outright at home to the Arizona Cardinals while the Indianapolis Colts (seven-point favorites) lost an AFC South battle with the previously winless Tennessee Titans. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. Kyler Murray should be able to produce enough offense to let his defense lead them to a win in this interconference duel. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. They’ll be returning to U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7 to host the Indianapolis Colts, and the folks who get paid to set the betting odds seem to think that they’ll emerge from that game unscathed. Our friends from the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 7 in the NFL, and the Vikings are starting the week as a 5.5-point favorite over the Colts. The over/under for this one has started out at 42.5 points. The Colts had a bit of a rough week in Week 6, as they fell to the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium by a score of 26-20. It was the first victory of the season for the Titans, and the Colts couldn’t get out of their own way all afternoon. They turned the ball over three times, including a pair of interceptions from Daniel Jones, and also had a punt that was blocked by the Titans and returned for a touchdown. That’s how the Colts managed to lose despite holding the Titans to just 186 yards of total offense while blowing a 13-0 halftime lead on their home field. The Chiefs climbed to 5-0 by beating the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, while the Niners can get to 6-0 if they defeat the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The Vikings have done this despite being fairly anemic on offense, thanks to the performance of their defensive and special teams units. In their last game, they overcame two red zone turnovers to defeat the New Orleans Saints by a score of 23-13 in a game that they played without left tackle Christian Darrisaw and wide receiver Jordan Addison, and saw tight end T.J. Hockenson go out on the second play of the game with a concussion. The sportsbooks have spoken, folks, and the Vikings are pretty significant favorites to push their record to 6-0 this week when they face off against the Colts. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . away.blurb: Colts get bad news on Sauce Gardner amid calf injury after brutal Titans loss | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV Add Sporting News on Google div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> The Indianapolis Colts might be heading towards some major changes this season. Some change has already happened, with general manager Chris Ballard getting fired Monday morning. But he might not be the only one on the move this season. It might be a sell-off this year, even though they don't have their own first-round pick. The reason for that? The Sauce Gardner trade. That, too, has taken a bad turn, unfortunately due to an injury. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Gardner has a calf strain and is going to miss some time for the Colts. Indianapolis is going to be without their top cornerback going forward, as a challenged defense is going to be in a bit more trouble. Sauce Gardner has a calf strain, likely to miss time for Colts "More Colts news: Pro Bowl CB Sauce Gardner, who was unable to finish Sunday's loss to the Titans , has a mild calf strain that makes him week-to-week, sources say after the MRI," Rapoport reports. This update for the Colts' top cornerback is a massively unfortunate one. This mild calf strain is not season-ending, and it might not be an IR stint either. But, as Rapoport notes, Gardner is "expected to miss some time" as he recovers from this calf strain. Fortunately, it's not a lengthy injury. But the timing of the injury is really bad news for the Colts. MORE : Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching after ugly Titans loss Coming off a loss to the Titans, who came into the matchup at 0-5, the now 2-4 Colts are tied with the Houston Texans in the AFC South and face an uphill battle to make the playoffs. Add in that Daniel Jones hasn't looked as good as he did last season, the Colts just fired their general manager, and there's plenty of instability with this team coming off a loss to the Titans. Now, Gardner's hurt and will miss some time. Indianapolis is heading into Week 7 against the Minnesota Vikings , who are set to be without their top cornerback, which might lead Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison to have big days against an already leaky Colts' secondary. home.headline: Why Jordan Mason's return could be a game-changer for Vikings' offense
home.blurb: But in the fourth quarter, one finally hit. The Vikings made an adjustment, using a jet motion to take Cooper out of the play. Mason took a wide zone handoff to the left, patiently waited for his crease to open, and exploded through it for a 28-yard gain. A few plays later, Jones got into the end zone to give the Vikings their first lead of the day. Jones was a warrior in a workhorse role across four games without Mason, handling 97 touches and racking up 442 total yards. He played through pain. He helped the Vikings stay on schedule as an offense and stay undefeated. But that 28-yard gain remains the Vikings’ longest rush of the season. And for as good as Jones has been, they’re very excited about the looming return of Mason, who is expected to be back in action on Sunday against the Colts. “He’s gonna be shot out of a cannon in this game at the running back position,” O’Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday, noting that Mason has “fresh legs.” That excitement around what Mason can do in the Vikings’ 2026 offense hasn’t gone away during his month on IR, even with Jones playing as well as he has. This is going to return to a committee approach, and if Mason plays like the Vikings think he can, he might have a chance to emerge as the 1A option. It was almost cruel. The Vikings finally saw a breakthrough in the running game, featuring a player they were so excited about coming into the season. Then, over the next couple days, they learned that an injury suffered on that play would sideline the player for the next month. It was Week 1 against the Packers. For much of the day, the Vikings had struggled to get anything going with their revamped running game, no matter if Aaron Jones or Jordan Mason was carrying the ball. The Packers came in with a strong plan against Minnesota’s wide zone runs, sending linebacker Edgerrin Cooper on disruptive blitzes. Mason stayed in the game and later scored a touchdown of his own, finishing with 59 yards on 15 carries. But he reported some soreness in his thumb the next day, and after further evaluation, it was determined that he needed surgery and would miss at least four weeks. He was placed on IR. The Vikings are pretty certain that the injury occurred as Mason was tackled as the end of the 28-yarder. “We even saw it in the opener, on the play Jordan got dinged up on,” Kevin O’Connell said on Wednesday. “We had gotten off to a little bit of a slow start, some unscouted looks early on, some plays that the Packers made, but as the game went on, popping that long run that he did on wide zone. I think Jordan is — because we have Aaron, because we have the ability to keep him fresh but also let him keep leaning on the defense, he’s one of those backs that gets better as the game goes on. So I think we’ll see that.” One of the Vikings’ big focuses of this offseason was a run game that they overhauled after hiring former Dolphins OC Frank Smith to their coaching staff. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts' struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback. The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the NFL this season, kick-starting their franchise rebuild with an influx of rookies and second-year players. The team hopes to move from a consistently mediocre franchise that fights just to make a cameo in the playoffs to one that consistently battles for deep postseason runs. While the goal is lofty, the Dolphins have had to tear down their roster for 2026, taking a massive immediate salary cap hit to get the future cap under control. Development is the Dolphins’ name for the game, as they hope their young roster can learn and grow quickly. South Florida Sun Sentinel columnist Chris Perkins took a look at how Miami is hoping to speed along that learning curve with a weekly addition to the practice schedule: Every Thursday, after the Miami Dolphins conclude their regular practice, many of the second- and third-team players gather for a brief 7-on-7 session. It sounds minimal, but coaches and players say the extra work is helpful because it better acquaints backups on Miami’s offense and defense, offers more hands-on coaching, and familiarizes them with playing alongside the starters… “It’s been really important to me,” said [head coach Jeff] Hafley, who detests 7-on-7 sessions during training camp. “I think regardless of where you’re at, I think we’re still in a developmental league.” The 7 on 7s are only seven or eight plays, but the repetitions and additional coaching add up over the course of a season for Dolphins backup players, most of whom spend midweek practices playing on the scout team. And here’s the big thing: in the 7-on-7 sessions, backups run the Dolphins offense and defense, they’d run if they’re suddenly inserted into a game. When they play on the scout team during midweek practices, they run the opponent’s offense and defense. The Jets running back is dealing with a quad injury, but Wednesday’s absence does not establish his availability for Sunday. “He won’t practice today, and we’ll see how tomorrow operates to see how he goes during the week,” Glenn said. Glenn praised Hall’s approach to his recovery, saying he has attacked the process with the same intensity he brings to preparing for a game. Getting him back on the practice field would be an encouraging next step, but that remains something to monitor. Wednesday’s participation and injury designations come from the Jets official report . No game statuses have been assigned yet. Adonai Mitchell Working Back, Sunday Still Uncertain “Yeah, I would say that. I would say the pain tolerance deal,” Glenn said. “So again, we’ll see how that goes as the week goes.” Parham is also beginning to work his way back into practice. His progress bears watching as the Jets look to get healthier on offense heading into a division matchup. Mauigoa and Ossai Remain Week-to-Week Glenn described Kiko Mauigoa and Joseph Ossai as week-to-week. Both missed Wednesday’s practice, along with running back Kene Nwangwu. Omar Cooper Jr. Gives the Offense a Lift “I don’t want to say that it surprised me, but it was just good to see that we have another weapon back and doing the things that we expect him to do,” Glenn said. Thursday’s practice should offer the next meaningful update, particularly on Hall and whether Mitchell can increase his workload. home.blurb: Welcome to the Splash Zone, a collection of Dolphins stories from around the web curated for you each morning. You can check out more on that story, along with all the other stories here: Four Suggestions for the Dolphins Coming Out of the Bye – Alain Poupart, Miami Dolphins on SI The Miami Dolphins will return to action as one of the only two winless teams in the NFL The Miami Dolphins had rookie safety Kyle Louis return to practice Wednesday, opening up his 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve. Want to join in the conversation and share your thoughts or point of view on the Dolphins? Check out The Feed , our community-driven discussion about the Dolphins, football, or just about anything on your mind. You can find the feed on the front page of The Phinsider. Jump in now to advance the Dolphins discussion. The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the NFL this season, kick-starting their franchise rebuild with an influx of rookies and second-year players. The team hopes to move from a consistently mediocre franchise that fights just to make a cameo in the playoffs to one that consistently battles for deep postseason runs. While the goal is lofty, the Dolphins have had to tear down their roster for 2026, taking a massive immediate salary cap hit to get the future cap under control. Development is the Dolphins’ name for the game, as they hope their young roster can learn and grow quickly. South Florida Sun Sentinel columnist Chris Perkins took a look at how Miami is hoping to speed along that learning curve with a weekly addition to the practice schedule: Every Thursday, after the Miami Dolphins conclude their regular practice, many of the second- and third-team players gather for a brief 7-on-7 session. It sounds minimal, but coaches and players say the extra work is helpful because it better acquaints backups on Miami’s offense and defense, offers more hands-on coaching, and familiarizes them with playing alongside the starters… “It’s been really important to me,” said [head coach Jeff] Hafley, who detests 7-on-7 sessions during training camp. “I think regardless of where you’re at, I think we’re still in a developmental league.” The 7 on 7s are only seven or eight plays, but the repetitions and additional coaching add up over the course of a season for Dolphins backup players, most of whom spend midweek practices playing on the scout team. And here’s the big thing: in the 7-on-7 sessions, backups run the Dolphins offense and defense, they’d run if they’re suddenly inserted into a game. When they play on the scout team during midweek practices, they run the opponent’s offense and defense. away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable.
