away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. away.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. home.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
home.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.blurb: Ravens face crucial Lamar Jackson decision as Bengals prepare for his return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens face crucial Lamar Jackson decision as Bengals prepare for his return The Baltimore Ravens have received an encouraging update on Lamar Jackson after the quarterback returned to practice ahead of their clash with the Cincinnati Bengals. However, head coach Jesse Minter has yet to confirm whether the two-time MVP will be available. Jackson has missed time since injuring his left ankle against the Tennessee Titans. Baltimore have managed to remain competitive without him, but their recent defeat to the Cleveland Browns has increased the importance of his potential return. Tyler Huntley remains Baltimore's alternative if Jackson cannot return. He has thrown for 429 yards and three touchdowns this season, while also adding a rushing score. Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images Aryan Chadha Thu, October 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Ravens are now 4-2 and face a crucial AFC North contest against a Bengals side that knows how difficult Jackson can be to contain. Lamar Jackson's availability could shape Baltimore Ravens' clash with Cincinnati Bengals ESPN's Jamison Hensley reported that Jackson's status for the game remains unclear after he returned to practice. The quarterback was also seen walking with a limp as he entered the team facility. Minter confirmed that Jackson had been able to take part in some work but stressed that the decision would depend on his recovery. He said: "Again, it's a day-by-day thing, but he was able to get a little bit of work in and be involved in the preparation." The Ravens coach added: "I know this. When it's ready for him to be able to play, from both sides, and we feel like that's the best thing to do, that's what we'll do." Jackson injured his ankle during Baltimore's win over the Titans, completing 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before leaving the game. His record against Cincinnati makes his availability particularly important. Jackson is 11-2 against the Bengals, while Baltimore have lost all three games against them without him, according to Hensley. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has already made it clear that his team is preparing for the possibility of Jackson playing. "I think anytime you're going against a player like that, it's all hands on deck," Taylor said. "You've got to get him on the ground. He likes to extend a lot of plays." Huntley has shown he can cause problems for Cincinnati, recording 226 passing yards, two touchdowns and 54 rushing yards in their 2022 Wild Card meeting. However, the Ravens will be hoping Jackson's recovery progresses sufficiently to give them their starting quarterback for a game that could have a significant impact on the AFC North

Under league rules, that participation could have been limited to the team’s walk-through earlier in the day. He was listed as limited on the injury report. On their final injury report ahead of a Week 8 game against the Chicago Bears, they listed him as a full participant in that day’s practice, even though he only took reps with the scout team, an indication he was not ready to return from his hamstring injury. As for when Jackson will be ready to return from his latest ailment, Minter wouldn’t say for sure. Last season, hamstring and back injuries cost Jackson four games. In 2022, a knee sprain kept him out for the final six regular-season games and a wild-card playoff game. In 2021, he missed one game because of illness and the final four regular-season games with an ankle injury. home.blurb: Ravens face crucial Lamar Jackson decision as Bengals prepare for his return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens face crucial Lamar Jackson decision as Bengals prepare for his return The Baltimore Ravens have received an encouraging update on Lamar Jackson after the quarterback returned to practice ahead of their clash with the Cincinnati Bengals. However, head coach Jesse Minter has yet to confirm whether the two-time MVP will be available. Jackson has missed time since injuring his left ankle against the Tennessee Titans. Baltimore have managed to remain competitive without him, but their recent defeat to the Cleveland Browns has increased the importance of his potential return. Tyler Huntley remains Baltimore's alternative if Jackson cannot return. He has thrown for 429 yards and three touchdowns this season, while also adding a rushing score. Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images Aryan Chadha Thu, October 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Ravens are now 4-2 and face a crucial AFC North contest against a Bengals side that knows how difficult Jackson can be to contain. Lamar Jackson's availability could shape Baltimore Ravens' clash with Cincinnati Bengals ESPN's Jamison Hensley reported that Jackson's status for the game remains unclear after he returned to practice. The quarterback was also seen walking with a limp as he entered the team facility. Minter confirmed that Jackson had been able to take part in some work but stressed that the decision would depend on his recovery. He said: "Again, it's a day-by-day thing, but he was able to get a little bit of work in and be involved in the preparation." The Ravens coach added: "I know this. When it's ready for him to be able to play, from both sides, and we feel like that's the best thing to do, that's what we'll do." Jackson injured his ankle during Baltimore's win over the Titans, completing 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before leaving the game. His record against Cincinnati makes his availability particularly important. Jackson is 11-2 against the Bengals, while Baltimore have lost all three games against them without him, according to Hensley. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has already made it clear that his team is preparing for the possibility of Jackson playing. "I think anytime you're going against a player like that, it's all hands on deck," Taylor said. "You've got to get him on the ground. He likes to extend a lot of plays." Huntley has shown he can cause problems for Cincinnati, recording 226 passing yards, two touchdowns and 54 rushing yards in their 2022 Wild Card meeting. However, the Ravens will be hoping Jackson's recovery progresses sufficiently to give them their starting quarterback for a game that could have a significant impact on the AFC North

home.blurb: Lamar Jackson was listed as limited Wednesday with an ankle injury, while Cam Jurgens was a full participant as he continued working toward his Baltimore debut. Outside linebacker Tavius Robinson did not participate because of a pectoral injury. Jackson's designation was the biggest update after he missed the opening portion of practice available to reporters. Coach Jesse Minter later said Jackson got limited work, and the official report confirmed his participation. Rashod Bateman was listed as limited with a shoulder injury after exiting Sunday's loss to Cleveland. Bateman has 16 receptions for 233 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches producing first downs. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner also was listed as limited with a hand injury. Hibner has five catches for 70 yards and a touchdown. Cornerback T.J. Tampa, designated for return from injured reserve, was listed as limited with rest, toe, and ankle designations. He recorded 29 tackles, two passes defensed and an interception last season. Calais Campbell joined Robinson as the only nonparticipants, receiving a rest day. Mark Andrews and Trey Hendrickson practiced fully despite hand and finger injuries, respectively. Baltimore listed 15 players overall. Thursday's practice will provide the next indication of whether Wednesday's progress carries into the remainder of Bengals week. Tampa remains on injured reserve and has been designated for return. Jackson has missed two consecutive games after leaving the Tennessee matchup at halftime on Oct. 4. In four appearances, he has completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, posting a 119.6 passer rating. He also has 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Jurgens practiced without a red non-contact jersey and was listed as a full participant with a concussion. Full participation is encouraging, though it does not independently confirm completion of concussion protocol or availability against Cincinnati. Before the trade from Philadelphia, Jurgens played 242 offensive snaps this season, including 187 at left guard and 55 at center. Pro Football Focus charged him with 12 pressures allowed, including one sack, across 146 pass-blocking snaps. (Photo by Alex Davidson/Getty Images) | Getty Images l4blitzer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Quite a massive win for the Texans across the pond. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. The Giants, forced to start backup QB Jameis Winston since starter Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, decided to give recent trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy a chance in the 4th quarter. McCarthy went 11-of-21 for 243 yards for 1 TD and 1 INT, and had the Giants in position to possibly tie or win on the final Giants' drive of the game. The New York/New Jersey sports pages will have themselves a field day talking about the QB spot in this coming week. Likely because of that QB uncertainty, along with Houston's recent winning streak and the supposed talent disparity, the opening odds from FanDuel for the upcoming matchup between the Texans and the Giants are strongly supporting Houston at home: Overall, this may seem a bit high of an opening line. The Giants haven't played as difficult a schedule as Houston and they are coming in with key injuries and roster concerns. However, the Texans, even coming off a huge win against Jacksonville, are still struggling on defense and sit at 0-3 at home. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. away.blurb: The New York Giants took the field on Wednesday for their first of three practices ahead of a Week 7 game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas, this Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. Unsurprisingly, their list of the walking wounded remains long. The Giants have been one of the NFL's most-injured teams this season, although they have far more company around the league than they have in years past. On the positive side of the injury news, cornerback Paulson Adebo had his 21-day practice window opened. The Giants' full Wednesday injury report can be found below: CB Greg Newsome II (concussion) This article originally appeared on Giants Wire: New York Giants injury report: Paulson Adebo's practice window opened

away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. home.headline: Jaguars sign Jamal Hill to practice squad right after Texans cut ties with him
home.blurb: Running back Ameer Abdullah signed with the Jags in the offseason and ended up making the 53-man roster. He's since carved out a niche as a returner and as a third-down back. Safety Kaevon Merriweather landed on the practice squad when the season started but eventually joined the active roster . Maybe Hill could follow in their footsteps. The Jacksonville Jaguars weren't in particular need of help at linebacker but couldn't pass up the chance to add reinforcements at the position following their Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans. Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 reports that the Jags are signing linebacker Jamal Hill after he cleared waivers. The Texans just released him to free up a roster spot for wide receiver Tank Dell, who's close to playing for the first time since he suffered a devastating knee injury as a rookie in 2024. Circling back to Hill, he'll get to hone his craft in the Jacksonville practice squad but nobody would bat an eye if he ends up earning a spot on the 53-man roster at some point of the season. Why the Jaguars signed Jamal Hill to the practice squad after his Texans release The Jaguars have a well-rounded linebacker corps. Ventrell Miller and Foyesade Oluokun are firmly entrenched at the top of the depth chart. Branson Combs is the primary backup. Dennis Gardeck and Jalen McLeod are also in the mix but often leave the field on nickel packages to pave the way for a third corner. Jacksonville wasn't in immediate need of help at linebacker, but signing Jamal Hill makes sense when you take into account that the Atlanta Falcons claimed sophomore Jack Kiser off waivers. If the Jags suffer an injury at linebacker, they could easily promote Hill to the active roster or outright sign him. On top of that, you can bet that they liked his production and potential upside. A sixth-round pick of Houston in 2024, Hill had spent his whole NFL career with the Texans. He mostly saw playing time on special teams, and that's where he could potentially contribute in Jacksonville. Hill was a surprise roster snub on cutdown day but landed on the Houston practice squad once he cleared waivers. The former Oregon Duck was then signed to the active roster when fellow linebacker Henry To'oto'o suffered a shoulder injury that forced him to miss time. With To'oto'o and Tank Dell back in the fold, the Texans no longer had room for Hill, who'll get a fresh start with the Jaguars. Best-case scenario, he'll sign a reserve/future contract after 2026 and compete for a roster spot next offseason. Other players have had a similar path with the Jaguars the past two years. home.headline: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants
home.blurb: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel . Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here. Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Ryan Young Staff writer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally. Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Now Denver comes to Glendale with a defense that doesn’t give quarterbacks much time to get comfortable. The Broncos visit State Farm Stadium on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Kickoff is at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. Denver is favored by 4.5 points, and the total is 43.5. State Farm Stadium has a retractable roof, so we’ll have to see whether it’s open Sunday. For more matchups, check out our free NFL picks . Denver Broncos Have Been Winning With Defense Denver is 4-2 after beating Seattle 17-14 in overtime Thursday night. The Broncos haven’t been blowing anybody away offensively, but they’re winning games. That’s what matters in October. They had to grind out that one against the Seahawks, and the defense made enough plays to give them a chance. Denver has won four of its last five, and the two losses came against good competition. Sean Payton has to like where his team sits, even if the offense still gives him headaches. The Broncos have been getting after quarterbacks, and that’s a bad matchup for an Arizona offensive line that’s had trouble protecting its passer. Denver’s offense has been a different story. The running game hasn’t been dependable, and Bo Nix has spent too much time trying to make something happen with defenders in his face. The good news is he hasn’t been giving the ball away much. Against Arizona, Denver doesn’t need to get fancy. Run the ball enough to keep the defense honest, take the short throws, and don’t hand the Cardinals another afternoon of easy field-goal opportunities. The bigger concern is the secondary. Pat Surtain II has been dealing with an ankle injury, and Talanoa Hufanga has also been sidelined. Those are two important pieces when you’re facing a quarterback who can throw it around. Riley Moss has been bothered by a rib injury as well. Denver’s pass rush can cover up some problems, but not all of them. Arizona Cardinals Finally Got A Win Arizona is 2-4 after beating the Rams 18-16. The Cardinals were down 16-15 with less than a minute left before Jacoby Brissett got them into field-goal range. Ryland kicked the winner as time expired. That’s a nice road win, but let’s not pretend the offense was terrific. Arizona moved the ball for 338 yards and still couldn’t get into the end zone. Six field goals will win you a game once in a while. It’s not a great plan for the whole season. The Cardinals have been giving up too many points. Before Sunday’s win, they’d allowed at least 30 in four straight games. Denver isn’t a high-powered offense, but the Broncos can take advantage if Arizona keeps giving up long drives. The Cardinals also have trouble finishing their own possessions. Brissett can move the ball between the 20s, but somebody has to score touchdowns. Denver’s defense isn’t going to make that easy. Brissett completed 24 of 35 passes for 218 yards against Los Angeles. Bam Knight ran for 80 yards on 15 carries, and he gave Arizona some decent production on the ground. The Cardinals are still dealing with injuries, including James Conner and offensive tackle Paris Johnson Jr. Those are significant losses. Conner would give them a more dependable running game, while Johnson’s absence makes pass protection harder. That’s a rough combination against Denver’s front. Denver’s defense should make life difficult for Brissett, especially with Arizona having problems up front. The Broncos aren’t scoring a ton themselves, which is the part that worries me about laying more than a field goal. But I trust Denver to take care of the ball and make Arizona work for every yard. If the Broncos get a lead, the Cardinals could have a hard time catching up. Denver by a touchdown. Under 43.5 Points (-105) Give me under 43.5. Denver just played a 17-14 overtime game. Arizona scored 18 against the Rams, all on field goals. Neither offense has been particularly good at finishing drives. The Cardinals should struggle against Denver’s pass rush, and the Broncos haven’t been lighting up the scoreboard either. A couple of defensive turnovers could change things, especially if one gets returned for a touchdown. But I see a lot of punts, some field goals, and not much reason to expect 50 points. away.headline: Broncos-Seahawks report card: Once again, Denver defense bails out offense in win
away.blurb: After two long scoring drives that were a perfect blend of the pass and run, Denver’s offense was invisible in the second half. The Broncos gained two first downs, posted 30 yards, did not score and went three-and-out four times. They gained 32 yards on their last 10 drives, including penalties. It was a completely lackluster effort that wasted a defensive gem. If this is what Vance Joseph’s defense can look like without two All-Pro-caliber players in the secondary, watch out, AFC. Denver’s defense has put together multiple excellent games, but Thursday night was the unit’s watershed showing. On the boundary, the Broncos barely missed a beat despite Pat Surtain II being out with an ankle injury and Riley Moss barely playing because of a rib injury. Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron kept Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in front of them for the most part and held Seattle’s other options in check. Seahawks returner Rashid Shaheed did have a huge kickoff return and a few nice punt returns, though. Renck: It is time for Broncos' slumping Bo Nix to snap out funk. If not now, when? Branded Content Advertising by Ascend A relentless defensive effort saved the Broncos offense from a disastrous collapse If Broncos fans were told before the season their team would be 4-2, with wins over the reigning Super Bowl champions , the odds-on Super Bowl favorites, and the only team that beat them at home last year , they'd almost certainly sign up for that with glee. But what if you told them it would look like this: 2.9 yards per play, 3-of-14 on third down, a third-year quarterback rapidly regressing and an offense that's allergic to explosive plays. That's the conundrum in Denver right now, where the Broncos keep finding ways to win ugly. Thursday was the latest example, as Denver defeated the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 on “Thursday Night Football” at Empower Field. Here's The Denver Post's report card from Thursday night . Thursday was a reversal of the typical Broncos . Strong first half, dismal showing in the second. Bo Nix’s struggles are bordering on outright disasters at this point. He threw for just 107 yards on 17 completions — a strikingly low 6.3 yards per completion. A week after one of the worst games of his career, Nix followed it up with his fifth-lowest total. Denver’s wideouts are struggling to get open, as well. And while the run game showed flashes in the first half, it still finished with 2.6 yards per carry. J.K. Dobbins rushed for just 6 yards on six carries in the second half. The Broncos keep winning these games, but eventually their offense will need to hold up its end of the bargain. away.headline: Broncos injury report: Pat Surtain, Jonah Elliss, Talanoa Hufanga, Jonah Coleman updates
away.blurb: Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were limited while safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) and running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) did not participate. Surtain has missed the team's last two games, and it sounds like he might also miss Week 7 , but returning to practice is a good step in the right direction. Hufanga is likely going to miss at least one more game after sitting out last week's contest. Jahdae Barron and Taylor Rapp have done a nice job stepping up in the secondary while PS2 and Hufanga have been sidelined. Denver coach Sean Payton indicated Elliss avoided a season-ending injury , but he seemed to hint that Elliss could land on short-term injured reserve later this week. Meanwhile, Cooper is expected to return to the active roster this week after being reinstated by the NFL . Badie injured his thumb in the second quarter of last Thursday's game, and he was ruled out just before halftime. Meanwhile, Coleman is eligible to return from injured reserve this week, and he returned to practice on Wednesday, opening his 21-day window to be activated to the 53-man roster. The Denver Broncos hit the practice field on Wednesday as they begin on-field preparations for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals . Denver outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper ( reinstated last week ) and running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ) returned to practice, and cornerback Riley Moss ( ribs ) was a full participant. Elliss limped off the field late in the fourth quarter of last Thursday's game, and he was spotted wearing a walking boot and using crutches at a Colorado-Utah game two days later. It looks like Elliss will be sidelined for a bit after he wrote " Be right back " on social media over the weekend. Denver's scheduled to practice again on Thursday and Friday before releasing a final injury report with game statuses for Sunday. Social : Follow Broncos Wire on Facebook and Twitter/X ! Head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie's groin injury popped up after he "felt a little something" in his groin at the end of Thursday's practice. McDuffie did not practice Friday in what McVay indicated was a precautionary approach being taken. Safety Kam Curl (ankle) is also listed as questionable for Week 6, but McVay said they "feel good about him." McVay said Curl's ankle injury stemmed from "soreness" from Monday night's game against the Bills. McVay also said tight end Davis Allen (foot), who was limited in Friday's practice, is "trending in the right direction." Allen was later listed without a game status designation on Friday's injury report. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. Both offensive units boast elite fantasy firepower, but division clashes always bring unique defensive tests and gamesmanship. If you are navigating lineup decisions ahead of Sunday afternoon's kickoff, here is a breakdown of which Lions fantasy superstars belong in your starting lineup, and which options require a bit more caution. Must-Start Locks Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (WR1) * The Outlook: St. Brown remains the unquestioned heart of Detroit's passing attack. Operating out of the slot, "The Sun God" provides a relentless target floor that thrives in fast-paced divisional battles. Green Bay's secondary has struggled at times against refined route runners over the middle. Expect Jared Goff to lean heavily on his favorite target to sustain drives, making St. Brown an elite WR1 in all PPR formats. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (RB1) * The Outlook: Gibbs' dual-threat dynamic explosion makes him virtually matchup-proof. With his elite speed on Ford Field's turf, he only needs a handful of touches to break open a slate. The Packers have surrendered chunk plays to explosive pass-catching tailbacks out of the backfield, giving Gibbs immense ceiling potential in PPR and half-PPR leagues. High-Upside Starts Jared Goff (QB) * Verdict: Solid QB1 Start * The Outlook: Goff inside the friendly confines of Ford Field is one of the safest fantasy plays on the board. At home, Goff operates Drew Petzing' system with supreme efficiency and rhythm. While Green Bay's pass rush can generate pressure, Goff's quick-release capabilities and weapons across the field give him a safe 18–22 point fantasy floor with multi-touchdown upside. Start with Caution / Situational Starts Jameson Williams (WR) * Verdict: High-Risk Boom-or-Bust Flex * The Outlook: Williams possesses game-breaking speed capable of turning a single target into a 70-yard touchdown. However, against Green Bay's deep safety coverage, target volume can be volatile. If you need pure upside to pull off an upset in your matchup, roll the dice on Williams; if you require a steady double-digit floor, explore alternative options. Sam LaPorta (TE) * Verdict: Low-End TE1 / High-End TE2 * The Outlook: LaPorta continues to command valuable red-zone attention, but increased target competition across the offense has capped his weekly target share. Green Bay's linebackers and safeties play tough physical coverage against tight ends over the middle. He remains startable given the top-heavy nature of the tight end position, but manage expectations accordingly. Final Lineup Verdict Lock in your top-tier Lions stars without hesitation. Detroit's high-octane offense inside Ford Field provides plenty of fantasy production to go around. Fire up St. Brown, Gibbs, Goff with confidence as Detroit aims to defend home turf against their division rivals.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Lions predictions: Detroit's biggest weakness could decide Week 7
picks.blurb: Detroit scores points like no other, but also gives them up at an alarming rate. In other words, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should be salivating at the matchup. The fantasy managers who roster those players will be thinking the same thing. More importantly, this is a key contest in the ever-crowded NFC North where there is no margin for error. Green Bay enters the contest at 4-2, erasing any negative thoughts that surfaced after the 0-2 start to the year. Detroit is 3-2, which is good enough for last place in the NFC North. Both teams are chasing the 5-0 Vikings , with the 4-2 Bears standing in the way as well. With only so many playoff spots to go around, this Week 7 matchup could have massive implications down the road. Here's a look at the keys to the game, injuries to watch and a prediction. Lions vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Lions -142; Packers +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions Keys To Victory Slow down Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. It's easier said than done, of course, but it's the one true path to victory for Detroit - outside of winning a shootout. The Lions' secondary has been a huge weakness all season long, and perhaps there is no better team position to exploit that than the Packers. Green Bay will try to hit some home runs with its speedy receivers. Even with Brian Branch set to return, Detroit will have to be willing to sit back in zone coverage and hold the visitors to some singles. Packers Keys To Victory Stay patient. With a defense as weak as the Lions, the Packers just have to play the waiting game. And that's something Dan Campbell's teams haven't been known to do. Detroit can either take away the long ball or attempt to get to Jordan Love with pressure. If the Lions sit back, then the Packers need to show an ability to run the ball. If they pressure, get ready to light up the scoreboard. Green Bay has the advantage, but it can't beat itself. Injuries to watch • S Brian Branch • OL Cade Mays • OL Aaron Banks. Lions vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 34, Lions 30 This game might come down to who has the ball last. Detroit might be coming out of the bye with some reinforcements, but this is still a defense that will ruin a season. And for that reason, no lead is safe - especially against the rival Packers, who can strike quickly. Jordan Love was forced to grow up as a quarterback without a running game to rely on through the first six weeks. He is passing that test with flying colors after a slow start. Trust the more well-rounded Packers to get the job done and push their winning streak to four. Adam Kaufman: Lions 31, Packers 27 This should be fun. Green Bay has won three straight, but Detroit comes out of its bye with reinforcements. Brian Branch's expected return won't magically fix the secondary, though even a few additional stops could make a significant difference. The Lions already have an offense capable of taking advantage, with Jahmyr Gibbs headlining their weapons. Jordan Love should still find opportunities, and the Packers can absolutely win if they protect him and avoid giving the home team extra possessions. Josh Jacobs' availability is another important piece. I'm expecting both quarterbacks to have productive stretches. But Jared Goff and Dan Campbell have been a dynamic duo with extended rest and know what's at stake in a crowded NFC North. This should be competitive well into the fourth quarter, but I like the Lions indoors. Ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the Green Bay Packers saw an unusual amount of movement on the point spread. The Packers opened the week as underdogs, getting 1.5 points at most sportsbooks, but the line quickly flipped to Packers -1.5 by Monday morning. Then, once the dust settled and the game approached, at least a handful of books had switched back to having the Cowboys favored. The Packers cruised, however, earning a convincing 23-13 victory to move to 4-2 on the season. That record puts them in second place in the NFC North, 1.5 games behind the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and a half-game up on the 3-2 Detroit Lions. Both of those two teams were idle in Week 6, but the Packers have a chance to make some significant movement in the division next Sunday. Week 7 brings the Packers their third game against an NFC North opponent this season, as they will travel to Detroit to play the Lions in the late Sunday afternoon time slot. Look for that game to be FOX’s game of the week, particularly with the Packers’ recent resurgence back into serious playoff contention. However, the books are giving the Lions a reasonable advantage in this game thanks to it being played on their own home turf. FanDuel sportsbook opened the line at Lions -3.5 for next Sunday in the first of two meetings between these teams in 2026. Books are also expecting another high-scoring game between these two squads, setting the over/under for total points at 52.5. Last year saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time since Dan Campbell took over as Lions head coach. Green Bay took the season opener at Lambeau Field 27-13, then got another Thanksgiving Day victory in Detroit in a high-scoring, 31-24 affair. Prior to 2025, the 2020 season was the last time Green Bay went 2-for-2, when they won similarly high scoring games in weeks 2 (42-24) and 14 (also 31-24). away.headline: Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Jordan Love’s Ailing; Here’s What He Said
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers’ star quarterback, who has carried the load for most of the team’s 4-2 start, was deemed limited participation on Wednesday, the first day of on-the-field work before Sunday’s NFC North showdown at the Detroit Lions. Only one player, receiver Bo Melton (back), would not have practiced. Nine players were limited, including Love and receivers Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Christian Watson (ankle). The Lions are coming off their bye. Every player on the roster practiced, including safety Brian Branch, who is set to return from last year’s torn Achilles. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), QB Jordan Love (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Limited participation: CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring). GREEN BAY, Wis. – Jordan Love has taken a beating at times this season. For the first time, it’s shown on the injury report. He said “no” when asked if he was concerned that he will not be in the lineup against Detroit. Coming off a Sunday night game and with a Thursday night game looming against the Panthers, coach Matt LaFleur conducted a “jog-through” practice on Wednesday but will put the team in pads for a “really good” practice on Thursday. That was welcome news for Love. After two games of strong pass protection in wins over Tampa Bay and Chicago, it was another painful week for Love in the win over Dallas. “It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” he said. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.” By the official stats, Love and Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson have absorbed a league-high 45 hits through Week 6. He was hit eight times and sacked on three against the Cowboys. “Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. away.headline: Jordan Love Headlines Packers Injury Report Alongside Christian Watson and Matthew Golden
away.blurb: That said, star quarterback Jordan Love was listed as a limited participant due to a back injury. Not only that, but his top wide receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, were both listed as limited participants as well. Seeing Watson's name on an injury report is never good, knowing what he's dealt with in his career. He was listed as limited due to an ankle injury in this one, while Golden is dealing with an apparent shoulder injury. Offensive guard Aaron Banks was listed as limited due to a knee/toe injury, but thankfully he was the only offensive lineman on the report. Defensively, cornerbacks Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck) and Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) were both limited. Defensive tackles Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Jordon Riley (Achilles) were also limited. Remember, Riley is currently in his 21-day practice window after coming off the IR. The only player to be listed as "did not participate" was WR Bo Melton (back). Fellow wideout Savion Williams (ankle) was also limited. Jordan Love Headlines Packers Injury Report Alongside Christian Watson and Matthew Golden - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz Wed, October 21, 2026 at 8:35 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers ' initial injury report on Wednesday, Oct. 21, revealed quite a bit of new information. It should be noted that the Packers didn't officially practice, so these are all just estimations. In the biggest surprise of the week, running back Josh Jacobs didn't see his name on the report, so he should be a full-go in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. It's not like Love necessarily got obliterated by the Dallas Cowboys, but he was sacked three times, one of which was by his former teammate, Kenny Clark. Love has been sacked 13 times in six games this season, and he also tied his season high with four carries on Sunday Night Football. Green Bay has always been careful about using him in the run game, but they dialed up a perfect zone read against fellow former Packers defender Rashan Gary. Packers fans must take a deep breath because this back "injury" is only an estimation, and head coach Matt LaFleur made it clear the team is trying to do everything they can to stay healthy coming off a primetime game with Thursday Night Football looming on Oct. 29. To say not having either Golden or Watson on the field is alarming would be an understatement. This is one of, if not the most dynamic receiving duos in the entire league right now, and each had a big drop or two against the Dallas Cowboys, but the team's confidence in them, specifically Golden, is through the roof.

The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. home.blurb: "Well there's some things that we took out of that. I think in all three areas, some things that we feel like we can do more of. Some things that we need to pull out. home.blurb: But there are some concerns at the moment regarding the statuses of some of their key players, including quarterback Jordan Love and wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Love said that he is dealing with a sore back, but he allayed fears on his availability for Week 7's game against the Detroit Lions by saying that there's no chance he'll not suit up for that contest against an NFC North rival, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Meanwhile, the statuses of Watson and Golden also don't seem to be something to be overly concerned about, at least for now. Watson and Golden have been Love's top targets downfield in the 2026 season. The 27-year-old Watson is leading the Packers with 538 receiving yards to go with six touchdowns on 29 receptions and 48 targets. The speedy Golden, on the other hand, is having a breakout campaign. The 23-year-old former Texas Longhorns star wideout has 501 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 30 catches and 57 targets to his name through six weeks of football. Given how bad the Lions' pass defense has been thus far in the 2026 season, Green Bay has a great opportunity to showcase their passing attack. Detroit is allowing 297.4 passing yards per game — the worst in the NFL. picks.headline: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams
picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.blurb: Having a 2-4 record six games into the season was not on the Bingo cards of most Los Angeles Rams fans. The team has been hit hard with injuries. Edge-rushers Myles Garrett and Kobie Turner, defensive tackle Poona Ford, and tight end Terrance Ferguson are all on injured reserve, and star wide receiver Davante Adams joined them after suffering a hamstring injury in Sunday’s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Fellow receiver Puka Nacua has also dealt with injuries this offseason, and with the Rams’ passing offense struggling this season, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay believes they should make a move now to add another premier wideout. Kay recently wrote the Rams should sign free-agent WR Tyreek Hill, whose agent Drew Rosenhaus recently told reporters his client was close to signing with another NFL team. “With Adams expected to miss six to 10 weeks while he recovers from a ruptured hamstring, the Rams need to offset the loss of their star wideout with a pickup on the open market. No free agent can move the needle more than Tyreek Hill,” Kay wrote . “… Hill’s résumé makes him an intriguing potential replacement, although his recovery and lengthy absence create uncertainty about how quickly he could contribute…. If healthy, his speed, route-running and elusiveness could help Los Angeles replace some of Adams’ production.” Replacing Adams’ production won’t be easy. Through six games, he totaled 30 catches on 49 targets for 480 yards and four touchdowns. He ranks eighth in receiving yards, 16th in receptions, and he’s tied for sixth in touchdowns. While Hill is no longer in his prime, he could still be a serviceable target for Matthew Stafford. In 10 seasons, Hill has totaled 819 catches, 11,363 yards, and 83 touchdowns. He had six 1,000-yard seasons in seven years from 2017 to 2023, and Hill could be a strong WR3 once Adams is back healthy. home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
home.blurb: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal." Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season. While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum. "C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line." Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media. "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game." The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

Brock Purdy and his offense struggled without Evans during the second half of Monday night’s win against the Commanders. They nearly blew a 20-point advantage due to their inability to gain first downs and kill the clock. To make matters worse, Deebo Samuel Sr. is also currently sidelined, which could leave Purdy with veteran Brandin Cooks as his top wideout. San Francisco is going to need firepower to keep pace with the pesky Falcons, who are led by Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Mike Kadlick Week 7 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+190) vs. New York Jets It’s time for the Dolphins to notch their first win of the Jeff Hafley era. While Miami currently owns the NFL’s worst offense and a bottom-10 defense, they’re coming off a bye week and are playing a Jets team that has lost four of its last five games. Though they’ve played competitively for the most part, New York has still yet to find an identity under coach Aaron Glenn and could be ripe for the taking after losing to the Patriots in Foxborough in Week 6. I think Miami finds their way to victory on Sunday at MetLife. Iain MacMillan Week 7 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+140) vs. Carolina Panthers It's time to sell high on this Panthers team. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face. Once they started facing top-10 defenses, I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate. I'm going to get in on the Bucs early this week and hope that Baker Mayfield ends up returning to action. If he starts on Sunday, we'll likely get some nice closing line value on the Buccaneers. Peter Dewey Week 7 Upset Pick Kansas City Chiefs (+124) vs. Seattle Seahawks This may be the biggest test for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs so far this season, as Seattle has the No. 1 defense in yards per play allowed and the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play. Yet, I’m taking Kansas City to win outright on the road and improve to 6-0. The Chiefs have found a new dynamic with Kenneth Walker III and this running game, and I expect the reigning Super Bowl MVP to have a major workload against his former team. Mahomes is a shocking 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up as a road underdog in his career, and he’s by far the better quarterback in this game. Sam Darnold has doomed Seattle at times this season, throwing seven picks in four games since returning from a glute injury. The Seahawks offense has been extremely reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and it ranks 25th in the league in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate.
