Walker, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs visit the Seahawks (3-3) on Sunday night. Walker leads the NFL in rushing with 665 yards despite already taking a bye week while the Seattle has missed the Super Bowl MVP. The Seahawks are 18th in rushing and have averaged 3.9 yards per attempt. Sam Darnold has seven interceptions in slightly more than four games and the Seahawks haven’t made up for Walker’s absence. But they have Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL with 717 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. Walker has provided the Chiefs a balanced attack. They haven’t had a 1,000-yard rusher since Mahomes became the starter in 2018. Walker is on pace for 2,261 yards, which would set a single-season record. Despite their struggles, the Seahawks are 2 ½-point favorites. Pro Picks likes the home team. Caleb Williams was nearly flawless in his first game back, leading the Bears to 31 points. Chicago plays consecutive primetime games against last season's Super Bowl opponents, starting with the Thursday night matchup. Baltimore is eighth in rushing and relying on Derrick Henry is a smart move if Jackson is out. They’ve been winning on defense and special teams and need Kyler Murray to get the offense going. Atlanta is 3-2 ATS in past five games against San Francisco. picks.blurb: The dynamic running back broke free of his platoon in Washington state after being deemed expendable despite the Seahawks' $700 million in contract extensions to keep its core intact. That made him the balm in a terribly burned Kansas City Chiefs backfield, where he's put up an Offensive Player of the Year pace across the team's 5-0 start. Now he faces his former team in his former home in primetime. That game has us torn in Week 7. It's not the only one. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 7 picks. Patriots at Bears Steelers at Saints Bengals at Ravens Browns at Titans Colts at Vikings Dolphins at Jets Giants at Texans 49ers at Falcons Bucs at Panthers Broncos at Cardinals Packers at Lions Rams at Raiders Chiefs at Seahawks Cowboys at Eagles Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: New York Jets (-4.5) over the Miami Dolphins Cool, I've murdered you once again. While I appreciate some Indianapolis Colts schadenfreude, I'm truly not enjoying this year's survivor slate. Ah well, time to back another flawed team with a quarterback working through yet another redemption arc. The Dolphins are coming off a bye and scored 24 points their last time out, but that was also the only week this season in which they've topped 13. New York's defense is competent. The Jets offense just got a boost with Omar Cooper Jr. returning to the lineup. Geno Smith faces the league's second-worst passing defense. If he can't thrive here, it's time to fade back into "high value backup" status. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 3-3 Hardest favorite to back: Baltimore Ravens (-1.5) over the Cincinnati Bengals Oh, friends, do I ever hate this pick. We're writing this on Wednesday and don't know what Lamar Jackson has planned for the week. If he's playing? I'm in. If not? This flips to Joe Shiesty and company. But, for now, let's assume we get an 80 percent Jackson behind center. Why I like this pick : The AFC North isn't defined by logic and answers only to the gods of chaos and violence. Baltimore has fielded the slightly better defense, and an emerging Ja'Kobi Lane brings an important fallback option. The Ravens find an extra gear against Cincinnati, beating the Bengals five of their last six tries and scoring at least 24 points in each of those wins. Why I don't like this pick : Even if Jackson plays, he'll have to face a revitalized and suddenly viable Bengals pass rush that has a strategy beyond "throw Trey Hendrickson at them, hope it works." The Bengals have the manpower to blitz effectively and the defensive backs to stand up in single coverage. Baltimore's top-heavy receiving corps will be put to the test, and it may take a Lane or a Devontez Walker to lift this team up in a high-scoring affair. Those Ravens wins came under Jim Harbaugh. Jesse Minter might be able to take up his mantle, but those are big shoes to fill seven weeks into his rookie season. Even worse, Cincinnati is coming off a bye. Season to date : 5-1 Upset pick of the week: Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) over the Seattle Seahawks Kenneth Walker III's respectful revenge game! The reigning Super Bowl MVP has been masterful at unclogging a previously stagnant Chiefs offense. Now he faces a defense he knows well. Will he leave Lumen Field with yet another win? The Chiefs are rolling right now. The Seahawks are not. The Super Bowl mainstay has rebounded from its uncharacteristic 2025 falloff by letting Walker cook. Kansas City has a top 10 passing offense in terms of expected points added (EPA) but is No. 1 by a wide margin when it comes to the run game . The Seahawks' run defense ranks third, which means this game is probably gonna be a pleasant reminder why we love this dumb sport so much. But Kansas City can counter with Patrick Mahomes. The Seahawks have Sam Darnold, who appears adrift without former coordinator Klint Kubiak, now head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders . Darnold's -0.050 EPA per dropback ranks 28th in the league. He's struggled to connect with anyone not named Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Chiefs have fielded a top four passing offense this season. The Seahawks are at home and facing a breaking point when it comes to the NFC West race. Dropping under .500 could give the San Francisco 49ers a four-game lead in the division, and while there are still 10 games to be played for both teams, that's a deep hole to dig out of. Seattle's fans understand that, and they're going to be LOUD as evening descends on the Emerald City. The Chiefs have gotten better returns than expected from their receivers, but asking Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals to shine against the Seattle secondary is a monumental ask. Even in a 3-3 start the Seahawks defense ranks second only to the Minnesota Vikings in overall efficiency through six weeks. away.blurb: Afternoon update: Despite not receiving a pre-practice designation from Reid, Simmons was not seen at practice, according to numerous reports . Later in the afternoon, Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest reported that Simmons would be listed as "DNP (back/personal)." Simmons returned to practice in a limited capacity last week as a part of his recovery and ramp-up process from his back injury- later described as a bulging disc -that first appeared late in training camp . Simmons participated in all three practices last week but was a limited participant each time. Moore left Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers due to a concussion that kept him out for the game's second half . While Moore navigates the concussion protocol, offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu is expected to be the first man up at right tackle, as he finished the game in Moore's place against LA. The Chiefs made a flurry of linebacker-based roster moves on Wednesday, designating linebacker Cooper McDonald to return to practice after a short stint on the injured reserve list. McDonald was placed on IR due to a knee injury suffered early in KC's Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos. away.headline: Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III will test Seahawks in return to Seattle
away.blurb: Charbonnet, who sustained a torn ACL that required surgery in a divisional-round playoff victory last season, was a full participant in practice Wednesday and might be able to return this weekend. Seattle's ground game has struggled without Charbonnet and first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest/shoulder), who has been on injured reserve since Week 2. Seahawks starting weakside linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle), who sat out last Thursday, missed practice on Wednesday. Fellow linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique) and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) were among the players who were limited. Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) also missed practice. It remains unclear when left tackle Josh Simmons (back), who sat out Wednesday, will make his season debut. The NFL's top rusher will lead his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), into a primetime matchup Sunday against the defending NFL champion Seahawks (3-3), for whom he won the Super Bowl MVP award last season. "I'm just focused on critiquing the mistakes we made," said Walker, referring to last weekend's sluggish 22-6 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. "Once we get to that point (Seattle), we'll see." For the soft-spoken Walker, that wasn't surprising. But others, on both teams, had plenty to say. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him to get back to the place where you kind of built your career and won a Super Bowl," Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. " ... But at the end of the day, we have to win a football game." Seahawks safety Julian Love said it's been "weird for sure" watching film of Walker break off long runs for the Chiefs. "He's doing what he did for us last season, the past bunch of seasons for the Seahawks. And he's picked up where he left off from last season," Love said. "His tape looks incredible. And so it's all hands on deck to try to contain and try to stop him." Walker, who signed a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Chiefs in the offseason as a free agent, leads all NFL running backs with 665 yards rushing and 6.3 yards per attempt. His six rushing touchdowns are two behind Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, though he's played in one fewer game because of Kansas City's early bye week. Walker rushed for 135 yards on 27 carries in the Seahawks' 29-13 victory against New England in the Super Bowl. home.blurb: Emanuel Wilson led the way with 14 carries in Denver, while George Holani out-snapped him 49 to 27 and posted an 83.3 rushing grade on six runs, according to PFF. Jadarian Price ran for 119 yards on 28 carries in three games before landing on injured reserve with a chest injury, and his fumbles before the IR stint are part of the concern. Zach Charbonnet is still on the PUP list after February ACL surgery. For a team trying to make up for losing Walker , Barkley is the biggest name available, but CBS conceded the price would be steep given his value and cap hit. He has 182 yards on 36 carries in four games while dealing with a hamstring injury, and the Eagles' run game sits at minus-0.18 EPA per rush on Sumer. Philadelphia is also 2-4 with Jalen Hurts out for the season, which is why CBS thinks the Eagles should take calls. home.blurb: Leading into Week 6, the Chiefs had starting left tackle Josh Simmons back at practice in a limited capacity for all three sessions . Before last week, Simmons hadn't practiced since Aug. 16. Asked about his potential status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Reid was hesitant to overpromise. The team will continue to ramp up Simmons' workload and see how he responds as he returns from injury. The Chiefs could realistically be without two of their most experienced offensive tackles, Moore and Simmons. That would leave Kahlil Benson as the starting left tackle and Joshua Ezeudu as the starting right tackle. Diego Pounds would also be active for the first time since Kansas City acquired him in a trade , should Moore be out with his concussion. Reid discussed Ezeudu's Week 6 performance on Monday. The trade acquisition filled in for Moore after the concussion just before halftime against the Chargers. “I appreciated the guys and how they played yesterday,” Reid said “Josh (Ezeudu) jumped in and played at the right tackle spot. I thought he did a nice job there. So, and he's got experience. I'm not real worried about all that.” In 17 pass-blocking snaps on Sunday , Ezeudu allowed just one hurry per Pro Football Focus. The Chiefs put him in a good spot to be successful in that game. With a full week of practice and preparation as a potential starter, Ezeudu could deliver an even better performance against Seattle. Moore could realistically practice and play this week. It's not out of the question. It's happened before. However, concussions typically mean that you're slated to miss at least one week of the season. An independent neurologist must clear him before he can return to play. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs trade acquisition in line for his first start as offensive line injuries linger into first practice for Week 7 vs. Seahawks
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs could trot out a third starting offensive line combination of the 2026 NFL season in Seattle. Wednesday's practice offered few encouraging signs for a pair of injured tackles. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed Wednesday that starting right tackle Jaylon Moore remains in the NFL's concussion protocol . Moore must clear the league's return-to-play protocols to suit up against the Seahawks. According to Reid, he would not participate in Wednesday's practice. What Are the NFL's Return-to-Play Protocols for Concussions? Players placed in the NFL concussion protocol must complete five phases without symptoms before they can be cleared to return to play. Symptom-limited activity: Light stretching and stationary bike riding. It remains to be seen whether Moore can clear those protocols ahead of the Week 7 matchup. However, sitting out of practice entirely on Wednesday isn't a good start. So who is in line to start at right tackle? Fans would hope starting left tackle Josh Simmons could return to the lineup after he practiced in a limited capacity ahead of Week 6's game against the Los Angeles Chargers. That didn't look promising on Wednesday. Reporters didn't spot Simmons on the field during their brief look at team stretch and warm-ups. Reid also didn't mention Simmons' status when he addressed injured players. He spoke only about Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice, who also did not practice. Simmons did return to practice in a limited capacity last week. Still, clips captured during the brief window the team gives media members ahead of practice made it clear Simmons wasn't 100%. He was seen grimacing while stretching , and he simply didn't look right while jogging on the field. It very much looks like the back injury will keep him out longer. Reid's comments on Monday suggested the Chiefs are continuing to work through his back issue while ramping up his workload. Again, missing practice Wednesday doesn't set him up for a likely Week 7 return. The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. picks.headline: Eagles vs. Cowboys prediction as Philadelphia adjusts without Jalen Hurts
picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys were figured to be the two frontrunners in the NFC East this season, with some even considering the duo as Super Bowl contenders. Just six weeks into the season, both teams are closer to booking vacations than they are preparing for a February trip to Los Angeles. Injuries did a number on the Eagles, claiming Saquon Barkley and many more. Recently, Jalen Hurts was added to that list. The quarterback is done for the year with blood clots . As for Dallas, it's still the defense. And it always has been. In recent weeks, though, the Cowboys offense has become a major problem as well. That isn't a winning combination for Brian Schottenheimer, who has seen his job security come into question lately. Both teams are desperate for a win, but at least the Eagles have a built-in excuse. Dallas will try to right the ship, but can they do it in a hostile Philadelphia environment? Eagles vs Cowboys odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Eagles -3 Moneyline: Eagles -162; Cowboys +136 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Eagles Keys To Victory Stay in the fight. For all intents and purposes, the Eagles season is over after it was revealed Jalen Hurts would miss the remainder of the campaign with blood clots. Injuries have mounted, but there is still talent on this Philadelphia roster. And with the way Dallas is playing, the Eagles just have to stick around long enough to let the Cowboys beat themselves. That leaky defense and anemic offense will give the home team plenty of opportunities to win. The Eagles just have to take them. Cowboys Keys To Victory Show up. On paper, Dallas should run away with this game against an offense that can't possibly keep up. However, the Cowboys looked disinterested in Week 6 and have looked that way for quite some time. This is the perfect get-right spot against a division rival. If the Cowboys don't beat themselves, they'll win the game. Injuries to watch • RB Saquon Barkley • OL Landon Dickerson • DL Jordan Davis • LB Nolan Smith • LB Jaylx Hunt • WR KaVontae Turpin • LB DeMarvion Overshown • LB Dee Winters Eagles vs Cowboys USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Eagles 23, Cowboys 17 The Eagles are injured. The Cowboys are lifeless. One of them has to win. How's that for a promo? Dallas is clearly the more talented team on paper, but something stinks about this group, and it's hard to pinpoint where the smell is coming from. The defense isn't competitive. The offense appears to be going through the motions. After a rough week for the Eagles, they should be motivated to stop the bleeding and get back in the win column. And what better way to do that than against a hated rival? Even if it's only for a moment, the home team finally gives the fans a reason to smile. Adam Kaufman: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20 Not sure how many times I'm going to put myself in position to be let down by the Cowboys this season, but here we are again. With Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles need Tanner McKee to stabilize an offense that was already having problems. Dallas' vulnerable defense – to put it kindly – gives him an opportunity, especially if Philadelphia can establish the run. On the other side, Dak Prescott's offense has been largely absent each of the last two weeks. But the superior talent undeniably belongs to the Cowboys and, if they can protect the ball, I like them to bounce back in a pivotal division matchup. away.blurb: After a string of running back moves, including Carson Steele going on IR, two running backs being waived or released, and Elijah Mitchell signing, Barkley might return this week . Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury, so his return would be massive. Hunt missed Week 6 after suffering a knee and ankle injury in Week 5. He may be able to return for the Cowboys game, but he could still miss another week or two. Dickerson is on IR with a knee injury and hasn't played since Week 1. Last week, his 21-day practice window opened for the first time, and he could potentially return for the Cowboys game to start at left guard again. Will Saquon Barkley return for the Eagles and help the running game? The Eagles have ran for just 57 yards in the last two games without Barkley. This season, he is averaging 5.1 yards per carry, showing that this Eagles offense is better at running the football with Barkley on the field. Hopefully, he can return and if he does, that might help the running game get rolling again. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender Skip to main content SI.COM As if everything else that has gone wrong for the Dallas Cowboys' defense hasn't been enough, the unit has also been ravaged by injuries to make matters worse. The Cowboys are missing starters at cornerback, safety and linebacker, and now they are in danger of losing yet another linebacker from the starting lineup. Last Thursday did not go as planned for Dallas, as the team suffered an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, but the team gets an opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 with another primetime showdown. This weekend, Dallas will make the trip to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Green Bay Packers . On Thursday afternoon, the Cowboys returned to the practice field and dropped their latest injury report . On Wednesday, five players did not participate in practice, but on Thursday, that number was down to two. Along with Overshown, Miller, and Speed improving their participation statuses on Thursday, there was another player who took a positive step forward: star cornerback Joey Porter Jr ., whose home debut was spoiled last week after a sudden illness. But after some extra time to recover from the issues that left him throwing up in the locker room before being sent home , he is feeling well and on track to play on Sunday night. Porter was listed on Wednesday's report with an ankle issue, but it is not serious, and he will be in line for an increased workload this week. Per reports, Porter is expected to have a "near full workload" in Week 6 . Hopefully, everyone will continue improving as the week continues, with just two days remaining until game day. away.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday. Packers Rule Out Four, Including Javon Hargrave Green Bay ruled out defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave , receiver Skyy Moore , and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste . Defensive tackle Jordon Riley , who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, is doubtful with an Achilles injury. Guard Aaron Banks is questionable with a knee and toe injury, along with defensive tackle Anthony Campbell with an ankle injury, cornerback Brandon Cisse with a hip injury added Friday, center/guard Jacob Monk with a quadriceps injury, and receiver Savion Williams , who has an ankle injury and is also in his return window. ‘I Just Kept Throwing Up’: Joey Porter Jr. Details Illness That Kept Him Out Against Buccaneers, Targets Green Bay A New Ankle Listing For Joey Porter Jr. Full Go For CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Smith, And Alijah Clark Safety Alijah Clark , who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, practiced fully all three days and carries no game status. So did left tackle Tyler Guyton with a back injury, outside linebacker James Houston with a shoulder injury, receiver CeeDee Lamb with a thigh injury, cornerback Shavon Revel with a knee injury, and left guard Tyler Smith with his surgically repaired thumb. Lamb said Thursday that his thigh bruise started in the second quarter of the Cowboys’ win at Houston and that he was back to square one after the mini-bye. Cornerback Keisean Nixon , edge rusher Lukas Van Ness , safety Evan Williams , and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt carry no game status. Micah Parsons , who is recovering from a torn ACL, is not on the report. Kickoff at Lambeau Field is set for 7:20 p.m. CT on Sunday, Oct. 18, on NBC. Save my name, email, and website in

away.headline: Four players questionable, two out for Dallas Cowboys; will Micah Parsons play?
away.blurb: Cornerback Cobie Durant will miss his fourth consecutive game and backup offensive tackle Drew Shelton will miss a second consecutive game with hamstring injuries, as both were ruled out on Friday. Even though head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Friday that linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a “long shot” to play with a hamstring injury of his own, he was officially listed as questionable after logging limited participation in back-to-back practices this week. He has missed four games since suffering the injury in Week 1. Trade acquisition cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been battling an ankle injury that limited him in practice on Wednesday and Friday. He was a full participant on Thursday. Fellow cornerback Ameer Speed has been battling a knee issue this week, but he was able to log back-to-back limited practices to finish the week. Both are officially listed as questionable. Rotational rookie defensive tackle LT Overton popped up on the injury report on Friday with a foot injury that prevented him from practicing. He is also listed as questionable. A quartet of players will not play for the Packers on Sunday night, as defensive tackle Jonathan Ford (calf), defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (achilles), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) were all ruled out on Friday. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley is working his way off the injured reserve list with an achilles injury, but he was ruled doubtful to be activated ahead of Sunday night. Five more players were listed as questionable, as defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip), interior offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quad), guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and wide receiver Savion Williams (ankle) will all be gametime decisions. Williams will need to be activated off injured reserve on Saturday to have a shot at playing. While the Micah Parsons return was something that was certainly on the table when this game was scheduled back in May, the five-time Pro Bowler has yet to return to practice as he continues to heal from a torn ACL he suffered last December. He will not be activated in time for Sunday night’s game and will instead be watching his current and former team square off from the sideline. He is expected to return in early November. Six players were listed on the injury report this week that all logged full practices throughout the week and do not carry a designation going into Sunday night: offensive tackle Tyler Guyton (back), safety Alijah Clark (hamstring), outside linebacker James Houston (shoulder), wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh), cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. (knee) and guard Tyler Smith (thumb). Four additional players were listed on the injury report this week but do not carry a designation into Sunday night: cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin), edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt (ankle). home.headline: Eagles not punished by NFL for handling of Jalen Hurts blood clots, per reports; NFLPA says more investigation needed
home.blurb: It was revealed Monday that Hurts will be out indefinitely after multiple clots were discovered in his lungs. The news came two days after Hurts was placed on injured reserve — despite initial reports stating the team wouldn’t place him on IR — and four days after last week’s announcement that he had a blood clot in his calf. “I fully trust the people that are involved in helping us all make these decisions,” Sirianni said. “We have great people here. … The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them. “Don’t have much more to say about that. That’s why we put the statement out. Full trust in those guys … kind of feels like you’re questioning that, and I know you guys have a job to do, but I’ve got the relationship with the players that I have because of the time that we spend together and because of the care that we have for each other. So, it’s always at the forefront of our mind.” The Eagles won’t face any heat from the NFL for their handling of Jalen Hurts’ potentially season-ending injury. The NFL concluded, in news first reported by The Athletic and later confirmed by the Associated Press, that the Eagles clearing Hurts to play in Week 5 despite having a superficial blood clot in his calf was “handled appropriately.” The league will not be issuing any punishment for their handling of the medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation for the game. Later on Tuesday, the NFL Players Association issued a statement: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” The Eagles’ medical staff has faced scrutiny from fans and media for its handling of the Hurts situation. Coach Nick Sirianni gave the team’s medical staff a vote of confidence Monday but declined to expand on the specifics of Hurts’ injury process. ©2026 The Philadelphia Inquirer. Visit inquirer.com. home.blurb: NFL Fans Demand 'Investigation' Into Philadelphia Eagles' Medical Staff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Andrew Holleran Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:49 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Eagles are likely to be without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, as he's being put on blood thinners, the team announced on Monday. Hurts missed this past Sunday's game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the team announced. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery." Hurts last played in a loss to the Jaguars in London. He threw for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports that Hurts stayed up for about 36 hours straight before that game, after being diagnosed. "How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? After initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, doctors told him not to sleep as a precaution, so he had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars, throwing for 220 yards and a TD," he reported. NFL fans, though, are shocked that the Eagles let him play in London. Fans are demanding a full investigation into how the team handled the Hurts injury situation. home.headline: Cowboys Injury Updates vs. Eagles: Turpin, Winters, Overshown
home.blurb: Both were hurt in Sunday night’s 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Turpin left after returning the opening kickoff 25 yards and was ruled out in the first quarter. Winters went down with 13:36 left in the second quarter, after he had intercepted Jordan Love late in the first. Turpin’s X-rays came back clean, according to Schottenheimer. Outside of those two, Schottenheimer said the Cowboys came out of Green Bay looking clean. He also gave a first read on linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , who has missed five games with a hamstring injury. KaVontae Turpin’s Rib Injury And The Dallas Cowboys Return Game Turpin is an All-Pro returner on both kickoffs and punts, according to DallasCowboys.com . Running back Tyler Goodson took over on kickoffs Sunday and had 5 returns for 122 yards. Receiver Jonathan Mingo returned 3 punts for 18 yards, including a 16-yarder to the Green Bay 46 that set up Dallas’ first touchdown after Green Bay went three-and-out to open the second half. Schottenheimer called that sequence complementary football and gave Mingo credit for catching punts in windy conditions. The staff will look at different options in the return game this week, he said. “I thought Goody did a nice job on some of the kick returns. We’ll look at some different things back there, how you want to do that. We usually do one with Turp. We’ll see kind of how that goes,” Schottenheimer said. “But, yeah, again, worth pointing out, Jonathan, that was a gusty night.” Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was in and out of the game Sunday after he rolled his ankle again. Porter had missed the Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness. Against Green Bay, he was targeted four times and did not allow a catch, according to DallasCowboys.com. “More of it was the ankle. He rolled it again, so he came out. And, again, I just love the way the guy played last night,” Schottenheimer said. “But, again, yeah, these guys feel their bodies pretty well.
